To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) volumetric CNNs are able to out-perform multi-view CNNs for object classification on ShapeNet; (ii) volumetric CNN architectures are able to out perform the current state-of-theart method on ShapeNet; and (iii) the best volumetric CNN architecture outperforms the current state-ofthe-art multi-view CNN method on ShapeNet.

(1) volumetric CNNs are better than multi-view CNNs in terms of accuracy, but are much more expensive, and (2) the best volumetric CNN architecture is the one that uses 3D convolutions, followed by 2D convolutions, while the best multiview CNN architecture is the 2D CNN architecture with multiresolution filtering. 3D CNNs are more efficient than 2D CNNs with multiresolution filters.

(a) volumetric CNNs are able to out-perform multi-view CNNs on the ModelNet40 dataset, and (b) volumetric CNN architectures based upon 3D convolutions outperform volumetric CNN architectures that are based upon 2D convolutions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multi-view CNNs are more accurate and faster to train, while volumetric CNNs are faster to predict and more robust to data augmentation.
volumetric CNNs are more effective for 3D object classification than multiview CNNs, and that volumetric CNN architectures are more effective than multi-view CNN architectures.

volumetric CNNs are the best approach to address object classification in 3D data, and that multi-view CNNs should be used only in special circumstances, such as when data is sparse and/or when data is not fully 3D.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to improve both volumeric and multi-view CNN architectures, and that the best performance is obtained by a combination of these approaches.
volumetric representations are more suitable for object classification on large 3D datasets, and multi-view representations are more suitable when 3D datasets are small.
we provide a new state-of-the-art for volumetric and multi-view CNN-based object classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of representation (volumetric vs. multi-view) is not as important as the choice of network architecture.
the performance gap between volumetric and multi-view CNN architectures is not due to the inherent limitations of 3D data, but rather due to the design of the network architectures.
volumetric CNNs can outperform multi-view CNNs on object classification.
